samir: hey team, getting a spike of 401s from a customer (Auth0) — they started failing ~10:12 UTC. error in logs: "jwt: signature invalid" and "kid not found in jwks". stack shows our auth middleware returning 401, no retries. any ideas? :rotating_light:

lina: oncall. can you paste a sample raw Authorization header (masked) + the exact error log lines? also which region/cluster is affected?

samir: sure. cluster: us-west-2-prod

samir: sample header: Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjEyMzQ1NiJ9.<payload>.<sig>

samir: logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z auth.go:142 error="kid not found in jwks" user=acct-8342 req=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z middleware.go:88 warn="token validation failed" code=401
```

sec-bot: alert: auth.401.rate +120% in past 5m for client_id: acct-8342

dmitri: probable causes:
- JWKS rotated at provider but our JWKS cache still has old keys (kid not found)
- provider rotated alg (RS256 -> ES256) and our validator only accepts RS* currently
- clock skew causing exp/nbf to fail, but your logs specifically say kid missing so start w/ jwks

maya: can you curl the issuer jwks from the Prod cluster node? sometimes CDN caching in front of jwks.json serves stale set.

samir: ran this from one of the pods:
```
curl -i https://auth.example-issuer.com/.well-known/jwks.json
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400
Last-Modified: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 04:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json

{"keys":[{"kty":"RSA","kid":"000000","e":"AQAB","n":"..."}]}
```

dmitri: that Cache-Control is suspicious — 86400s = 1 day. If Auth0 rotated keys, our cached set could be missing the new kid. Our runtime has jwks_cache_ttl configured to 300s but we rely on conditional GET for refresh; if upstream returns long max-age, our client might respect it. also we do not refetch on "kid not found" right now (bug).

alex: +1. we had a similar incident where CloudFront cached the jwks and fronted it with long TTL. two mitigations:
- tolerate provider Cache-Control but add heuristic: if validation fails with "kid not found", fetch jwks again (bypass cache)
- implement background refresh: fetch jwks every Xs regardless of cache-control

lina: steps to reproduce requested by support: can we craft a token using a new key (different kid) and confirm our validator rejects it with current code, then patch and confirm accepts after refetch? small repro in sandbox will be helpful.

dmitri: repro steps I used:
1) curl provider jwks and save as old_jwks.json
2) provider rotates keys (or simulate by generating a token signed with a new key that isn't in old_jwks)
3) run our validator binary in sandbox (bin/auth-validate) with --jwks-url pointed at local file server that serves old_jwks.json with Cache-Control 86400
4) send token -> validator returns "kid not found"

example token decode snippet I used (header):
```
{"alg":"RS256","kid":"new-key-01"}
```

maya: also check clock skew — if provider issues tokens with slightly different nbf/iat and our host clocks drifted, you'll see 401s with exp/nbf errors. look at /var/log/chrony on the hosts. but again logs were kid-not-found so lower priority.

samir: i ssh'd into one of the app VMs and chrony shows step >30s applied last week. some older VMs had time drift. i'll check.

alex: one more edge: some providers publish jwks with JWKey entries missing 'kid' or with 'x5c' only. our validator expects kid. if token arrives without kid header, we try to match by key material which we don't handle well.

dmitri: proposed immediate mitigation (hotfix):
- change validator to on-demand refetch when "kid not found" and retry validation once
- reduce effective jwks_cache_ttl to 30s for affected clusters
- add 120s clock leeway to JWT validation
- add logging: dump token header(kid, alg) on failure (PII-safe) so support can triage faster

lina: agreed. create a small patch, run unit tests, then a canary rollout to us-west-2-prod (10% traffic) and monitor auth.401.rate and latency.

samir: mock patch I tested locally (python pseudocode):
```
def validate(token):
    hdr = decode_header(token)
    if not jwks.has_kid(hdr.kid):
        jwks.refresh(bypass_cache=True)   # NEW
    return jwks.verify(token, leeway=120)
```

dmitri: extra notes:
- when provider rotates, there is often an overlap window where both old and new keys present. if provider removed old key immediately, clients with aggressive caching break.
- our runtime uses http client that honors Cache-Control by default. we should prefer conditional GET (If-Modified-Since / ETag) and also have a small max TTL override.

alex: ops action item: check any upstream CDN (CloudFront/Cloudflare) behavior for the issuer domain. add rule to respect origin cache headers but limit max-age to 60s for jwks paths.
